patch.value: Two residual admission gaps from the PR #1772 review: an inactive duplicate inline field can take over a built-in option, and a negated mutation flag passes harness output-control admission

Raised by the fifth Codex pass on PR #1772 (2026-11-23), not reproduced here; filed instead of extending a review loop that had already converged on the reported classes. (1) Settings writer: when inline settings hold two definitions for one key, the runtime registry uses the last one. A mutateWorkspaceSettings proposal that removes the winning definition activates the earlier one, and if that one shadows a built-in option (for example a flag full on list) the admission exempts it, because assertChangedSchemaFieldsAvailable (src/sdk/extension-command-context.ts) grandfathers any definition equal to some stored entry. Compare each proposed definition with the previously effective definition for its key, so only an unchanged active definition is grandfathered. (2) Harness: when an extension augments comments with a boolean --stdin declaration, runRegisteredCommandForTest accepts options { 'no-stdin': false, outputLimit: '1' } and runs the handler with stdin true, because the admission fold (foldOptionSpellings in src/sdk/testing.ts) keeps the negated key as noStdin while the normalizer applies the negation; native --stdin --output-limit 1 is refused with read_output_mutation_conflict. Apply the declared negation rules before deciding whether the invocation mutates. Duplicate check: searched duplicate inline field definition effective key admission negated mutation flag harness; pm-3s4jwl and pm-gh1769 (closed by PR #1772) own the main fixes.

A proposal that removes the winning duplicate inline definition is judged against the definition that becomes effective, with a spec seeding two definitions for one key; The harness refuses a negated spelling of a declared mutation flag combined with output controls exactly as native dispatch does, with a parity spec
Neither a duplicate inline definition nor a negated mutation spelling escapes the admission the native paths apply

value.text: Scope addition from the sixth Codex pass on PR #1772 (2026-11-23, P3, not reproduced here): schema add-field treats an explicit cliFlag that normalizes to nothing ('--') as omitted and silently drops a whitespace-only alias (normalizeAddFieldInput in src/core/schema/fields-file.ts), so the command succeeds with the default flag or without the requested alias, while the inline settings writer refuses the same spelling with schema_field_flag_invalid. Decide whether add-field should refuse an explicitly supplied empty spelling the same way; the same pass raised the duplicate inline definition and negated mutation flag cases again, both already in this item.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Two P3 additions from the seventh Codex pass on PR #1772 (2026-11-23, not reproduced here). (1) A field whose key is help but whose flag is another spelling (help-topic) is refused with schema_field_option_collision, because the key is compared with every built-in option including the implicit --help; the help option never supplies a parsed help value to the field reader, so only the flag and aliases should be compared with --help and -h, while the key check stays for built-ins that do supply parsed values. (2) runRegisteredCommandForTest builds the SDK through sdkFactory before output-control admission runs, so a factory sees global.outputLimit undefined for options { '--output-limit': '1' } while the handler sees '1', and the factory also runs for an invocation admission then refuses; resolve admission and the effective global controls before constructing the SDK.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Partly delivered in PR #1772 after CodeRabbit raised the same cases on c089f0d39 (2026-11-23): the harness now folds a negated boolean spelling of a mutation option (--no-add, no-add, noAdd with a boolean value) onto its base key as the normalizer applies it, so the negated-mutation case of this item is closed; and the SDK factory is built after admission, so it sees the resolved controls and never runs for a refused invocation (the second P3 above). Still open here: the duplicate inline field that becomes effective, the explicit empty add-field spelling, and the help key exemption.

value.text: Correction to the earlier note (2026-11-23): the negated-mutation fix in PR #1772 follows the option normalizer's rule (dashed no-<name> spellings of a declared boolean only), so it covers the declared --stdin case this item named. An undeclared native mutation key negated by a caller (for example --no-add on comments with no extension declaration) is passed through unchanged by the normalizer as well, so it is not a harness-native divergence.

value.text: Two harness-only additions from the final Codex pass on PR #1772 (2026-11-23, after merge as a5e8b5d3a; reported as reproduced by Codex, not re-run here). (1) annotationPositionalMutationOptions (src/sdk/read-output-contracts.ts) checks the command path before resolving it, so a harness call with command 'item comments' (or item notes / item learnings), args [id, text] and an output control runs the handler; native dispatch resolves the operation first and refuses. Resolve the path with the same resolver validateReadOutputOptions uses before the positional check. (2) The harness negation fold (negatedDeclaredBooleanKey and booleanToken in src/sdk/testing.ts) accepts only literal true/false and the long negated spelling, while the option normalizer also accepts 0/1 and case-insensitive trimmed tokens and a negation through a declared short alias; reuse the normalizer's spelling and boolean rules for admission. Both extend this item's harness-admission scope.

value.text: Fix (2026-11-27, branch fix/field-admission-diagnostics) for the five residual cases recorded here. (1) Settings writer: assertChangedSchemaFieldsAvailable (src/sdk/extension-command-context.ts) now also judges, per key, the definition the registry will read (the last resolvable entry) whenever it differs from the previously effective one, so a proposal that removes the winning duplicate and leaves an exact stored copy of an earlier shadowing one is refused with schema_field_option_collision; restating both stored entries still passes. (2) add-field and profile apply/lint: resolveAddFieldFlagSpellingDefects takes the supplied spellings, so an explicit --cli-flag or --alias that normalizes to nothing is refused with schema_field_flag_invalid (profile lint: field_flag_invalid) instead of being read as omitted or dropped. Through the SDK transport a whitespace-only cliFlag string is treated as omitted before it reaches add-field; filed separately. (3) Help key: resolveCommandCollisions judges a key spelled differently from every flag without the implicit --help option, because help exits before any handler reads a parsed value; key help with --cli-flag help-topic registers, stores values under help and leaves pm create --help working, while help as a flag or alias is still refused. (4) annotationPositionalMutationOptions resolves the command path with resolvePmHistoryOperation first, so a harness handler on item comments with positional text and an output control is refused like native dispatch. (5) The harness negation fold now calls resolveNegatedDeclaredBooleanOption (src/sdk/extension/command-options.ts), which runs the normalizer's own resolveNegatedBooleanSpelling over its spelling index, so 0/1, any case and spacing, and a negation through a declared short alias (no-S) count; a value the normalizer refuses is left for normalization to refuse. Specs: harness-parity, settings-field-admission and field-flag-spellings; with src reverted to main the four new cases fail.

value.negative_control: With src reverted to main the new cases in harness-parity, settings-field-admission and field-flag-spellings fail: the exposed duplicate is admitted, a blank add-field spelling is read as omitted, a help key behind another flag is refused, and the harness runs a namespaced annotation handler and misses 0/1 and short-alias negations

patch.value: Each admission path judges an invocation exactly as the consumer that applies it

The settings writer judges the definition the registry will read for each key; add-field, profile apply and profile lint refuse a supplied spelling that normalizes to nothing; a help key behind another flag is free; the harness resolves the annotation path first and folds negations with the normalizer's own rule

An exposed shadowing duplicate is refused with schema_field_option_collision; a blank cli-flag or alias is refused with schema_field_flag_invalid; key help with --cli-flag help-topic registers and pm create --help still works; the harness refuses item comments positional text and 0, 1 and short-alias negations beside an output control
The five residual admission gaps are closed with the same rules the consumers apply

value.text: Codex review round 1 (2026-11-27) on e02d401c0, verified and fixed: the settings writer compared effective definitions over the inline list only, while the registry reads the fields file after it, so exposing an earlier shadowing inline entry was refused even when a file-backed definition of the same key stayed effective. assertChangedSchemaFieldsAvailable now appends the fields-file definitions (readFieldsFileDefinitions, current and proposed fields path) to both sides before choosing the effective definition per key; a spec covers the masked case.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 (2026-11-27) on 9de3e2c90, verified and fixed: (1) the settings writer returned early when the proposed inline list was empty, so a proposal that cleared it and pointed schema.files.fields at a file with a shadowing definition was never judged; the early return is gone, and the fields-file overlay is compared on both sides. (2) The harness negation fold treated an empty negated list as a mutation; an empty list is zero occurrences, as normalization delivers it, so resolveNegatedDeclaredBooleanOption yields nothing for it.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 3 (2026-11-27) on 518645ca9: fixed: the harness negation fold now treats a negated list whose entries normalization drops (blank or nullish only) as zero occurrences, so it no longer refuses it as a mutation; a list with a kept entry is still a mutation. Deferred to a follow-up: judging against the hydrated registry when the current schema fails to hydrate.

value.text: Codex review round 6 (2026-11-27) on 3a88e434a, verified and fixed: when a file switch made a masked inline entry effective, the writer judged the proposal's normalized copy, which had already lost a blank alias that the stored entry keeps on disk, so the entry became effective without the empty-spelling refusal. The writer now judges the raw stored entry that resolves the same way, which is the spelling that stays on disk; a spec covers the unmasking switch.

value.text: Greptile review on PR 1790 (P1, 2026-11-27), verified and fixed: the round 6 lookup replaced the winning definition with any stored inline entry that resolves the same way, even when the winner came from the fields file, so a clean file definition was refused because of a masked inline entry, and a file definition with a blank alias passed when the inline entry was clean. The effective map now records each definition's source; only an inline winner is judged by its stored spelling, and a file-backed winner is judged as the file holds it. Spec cases cover both directions.

value.text: CodeRabbit review on PR 1790 (Minor, 2026-11-27), verified and fixed: two inline entries for one key can resolve the same way once a blank alias is dropped, and the stored-spelling lookup took the first match while the registry reads the last inline entry of a key; the lookup now matches from the end. A spec case keeps a masked earlier entry with a blank alias and a clean last entry, and the clean one is judged.

value.text: Decision after Codex review round 7 (2026-11-27): the raw-spelling lookup for newly effective definitions (added in round 6, refined after the Greptile and CodeRabbit reviews) drew a new edge case in each of four rounds, all about blank aliases on stored entries. Settled by principle instead of patching: the registry drops a blank alias, so it cannot shadow a built-in option or stop a command. A definition that becomes effective is judged as the registry resolves it, which catches every shadowing alias or flag; a raw spelling is refused only when it is newly supplied (the existing rule), and a stored blank alias stays a pm validate --check-metadata report. The raw lookup and its source tracking are removed; the settings-field-admission spec now pins the rule both ways (a stored blank alias becoming effective is admitted, a newly effective shadowing alias is refused, a newly supplied blank alias is refused). Codex round 7's two findings were both about that removed path.

value.text: Codex review round 8 (2026-11-27) on 0790dc02e, verified and fixed: the after side of the effective comparison read the proposal's raw inline list, while settings validation strips members the inline schema does not know (an inline value_schema) on every read, so restating an unchanged legacy entry with a value_schema and an alias shadowing --full looked newly effective and an unrelated write was refused, which main admits. The writer now builds the after side from the validated proposal, as it persists; the raw check for newly supplied spellings is unchanged. A spec restates such a legacy entry beside an unrelated change.
